item.title: Independent republics, castles and bagels: How to spend 24 hours in Vilnius, the capital of Lithuania
item.description: From strolling around the UNESCO-listed Old Town to reading the constitution of the independent republic Užupis, Lithuania’s capital city is perfect to explore in just one day.

item.title: Political earthquake in Serbia: The end of the Vucic Era and the rise of the student list
item.description: This is not simply a change of government. It is the collapse of a political order that has defined Serbia since 2012.

item.title: GPHG 2026: The 'Oscars of watchmaking' scraps gender categories for ‘a breath of fresh air’
item.description: Each year, the world's finest timepieces are celebrated at the Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève (GPHG) award ceremony, which marks its 26th anniversary on Saturday 7 November.

item.title: 'Having money is not enough': Why a job no longer guarantees access to housing in Spain
item.description: House prices rose 84.6% between 2015 and 2025, against 27.85% for average wages. Lack of affordable housing, rent burdens and saving difficulties deepen the crisis as experts call for structural reform.

item.title: Brazil's Lula clinches election victory as Bolsonaro rejects results
item.description: Lula's triumph bucks a regional trend of victories for right-of-center presidential candidates allied with Trump. It also means Latin America’s largest economy will likely continue defying Trump’s demands, despite the pressure of increased tariffs.

item.title: Serbia: crowds celebrate in Belgrade after Vučić admits defeat
item.description: Crowds celebrated in Belgrade after President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat for his ruling party in Serbia's snap parliamentary election, following nearly two years of student-led demonstrations.

item.title: Songs of praise: An emotional Greek-German musical collaboration at Berlin Cathedral
item.description: Thirty-eight students from the Chios Music School joined forces with choirs and ensembles from Berlin’s Song Academy as part of German Unity Day.

item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy confirms trilateral talks with Russia and US to take place in November
item.description: The trilateral talks aim to restart stalled peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, with the latter's invasion well into its fifth year.

item.title: Student List wins Serbian election in political earthquake as Vučić concedes defeat
item.description: The election was seen as a referendum on Vučić’s political dominance and the political system that had been in place in Serbia for more than a decade.

item.title: Marine Le Pen launches presidential campaign with vow to restore 'rule of law'
item.description: At a large rally in Orléans, the far-right frontrunner called for a "rebirth of France" and promised to restore "rule of law" after another weekend of protests across the country.

item.title: Brazil: long queues and river journeys mark decisive presidential vote
item.description: Brazilians headed to the polls on Sunday to choose between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. From canoe journeys in the Amazon to long queues in Rio and a Lula doll in Brasília, voters turned out for the presidential runoff.

item.title: Storms batter northern Europe, cutting power to more than 150,000 homes and disrupting road and air transport
item.description: Storms Austen and Boelo caused major disruption over the weekend across northern Europe with temporary power cuts to 150,000 homes, people in injured by falling trees and flights and ferries cancelled in several countries from Scotland to Denmark.

item.title: María Corina Machado back in Venezuela after 10 months in exile
item.description: The opposition leader was last in Venezuela in in December 2025, after which she left to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo. Since then, she has carried out much of her political activity from the United States and Panama.

item.title: Thousands of sheep take over Madrid's streets for Transhumance Festival
item.description: Over 1,400 sheep and goats took over Madrid's streets on Sunday, delighting spectators at the 33rd annual Transhumance Festival, which followed a different route this year to avoid a housing protest.

item.title: Off the Record: Yalta 2.0 spells bad news for Europe in desperate need of a plan
item.description: In this week’s newsletter Euronews’ Chief Europe Editor Maria Tadeo examines an “unfortunate triumvirate” facing Europe: Trump, Xi and Putin.

item.title: Demonstrators wounded as police break up Lisbon and Porto housing protest camps
item.description: The ongoing confrontation between police and protesters demanding affordable housing turned violent overnight. Police again moved in against protest camps in Lisbon and Porto in the early hours of Sunday, with several arrests and injuries reported.

item.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill four and injure 28, authorities say
item.description: Zelenskyy said on Sunday that Russia has launched roughly 1,600 guided aerial bombs, 48 missiles and nearly 2,300 attack drones against Ukraine over the past week.

item.title: Suspected Trappes gunman moved to police psychiatric unit
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron, who visited Trappes on Friday, has described the shooting as a "racist terrorist attack."

item.title: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham wants 'honest discussion' on return to EU free movement
item.description: Ahead of next month's UK-EU summit, Burnham said he favours an 'honest discussion' about the divisive issue of re-adapting free movement between the UK and the EU. But in an interview in London Sunday Times, he ruled out ever joining the Schengen zone or adopting the Euro.

item.title: Hellenic Basketball Federation president resigns amid match-fixing investigation
item.description: Liolios has denied the charges against him, and his defence team has argued that there is no solid evidence linking him to match fixing, describing the case as a conspiracy.

item.title: Israel orders West Bank crossings to close on election day following Hebron shooting
item.description: The move comes as part of a wider clampdown in the occupied West Bank after two Israeli soldiers were killed by Palestinian gunmen in the city of Hebron earlier this week.

item.description: The campaign has focused on Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and an increase in drone attacks on commercial vessels off Bulgaria's coast in the Black Sea, as well as rising energy prices and inflation.

item.title: Thousands march across Italy as protests bring isolated clashes with police
item.description: Demonstrations took place in Italy on Saturday over the rising cost of living. No serious clashes were reported, with nine people arrested nationwide.

item.title: Audi's first US production plant: carmaker strikes deal with Trump
item.description: Audi is planning its first car factory in the United States, with the Ingolstadt-based manufacturer set to invest billions in a new plant in Georgia.

item.title: More than 1,300 arrests across France as protesters clashed with police
item.description: Some 70,000 law enforcement officers were mobilised ahead of Saturday's planned protests after authorities bolstered security following last weekend's riots.

item.title: 128 arrested after night of unrest and looting in Barcelona
item.description: Protesters threw stones and other heavy objects at officers, whilst several groups erected barricades, set fire to rubbish bins and smashed shop windows.

item.title: Serbia goes to polls to choose between Vučić and student movement
item.description: The election is being seen as a referendum on Vučić’s political dominance and the political system that has been in place in Serbia for more than a decade.

item.title: Should Europe ban meat advertisements? We asked a climate psychologist to find out what would happen
item.description: As climate scientists call for a transition to plant-rich diets, could Europe’s streets lose their juicy burger billboards?

item.title: Graveyard tourism: Why Europe’s cemeteries are on the must-visit list for Halloween
item.description: From Jim Morrison’s grave in Paris to the overgrown Gothic tombs of London, these historic burial grounds offer an alternative to Halloween’s usual tourist attractions.

item.description: Young protesters clashed with police in Rome on Saturday as demonstrations over wages, the cost of living and public services spread across Italy.

item.description: Violence in earlier protests prompted authorities to take additional security measures, with massive deployments of police and even soldiers observed across several European capitals.

item.title: Brussels shops boarded up amid fears of repeat of last week's looting
item.description: Luxury boutiques and high-street retailers in central Brussels covered their windows with wooden panels to protect against possible looting as fresh protests raise concerns over further unrest.

item.title: Euronews on the ground as hundreds of thousands take to the streets of Paris
item.description: The government has blamed the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party and Jean-Luc Mélenchon for what it says is stoking violence, an accusation the party denies.

item.title: Rallies, opinion polls and a final debate - Brazil gets ready for Sunday's knife-edge presidential election
item.description: Lula against Flavio - both candidates in the second-round presidential election in Brazil hold rallies in major cities on the last day of campaigning. With around 20% of the electorate having abstained in the first round, the result is wide open and opinion polls show them neck and neck.

item.title: Israel removes around 250 Palestinian families from West Bank city of Hebron after soldier deaths
item.description: Days before tight elections are due to be held in Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has announced a massive operation on the West Bank after two Israeli soldiers were killed by militants at a checkpoint.

item.title: Fire engulfs Hitler’s former Eagle’s Nest retreat in Germany
item.description: A fire broke out at the Eagle's Nest, Adolf Hitler's former mountain retreat in southern Germany. Police say a suspect has been detained, and around 200 firefighters were deployed to tackle the blaze.

item.title: Violent protests shake Tirana as police use tear gas and water cannons against demonstrators
item.description: Opposition supporters and students mobilised in the Albanian capital, with riot police using water cannons on large groups of protesters. Authorities said 2,500 police officers were deployed to the streets of Tirana.

item.title: Watch: French police deploy armoured vehicles in Paris and Marseille
item.description: French police deployed Centaure armoured vehicles in Paris and Marseille on Saturday as authorities stepped up security during protests over the rising cost of living.

item.title: Italy: Thousands take to the streets as protests turn violent in several cities
item.description: Clashes erupted between protesters and police across several Italian cities on Saturday, with officers deploying water cannons and tear gas as demonstrations turned violent. item.title: Madrid joins weekend of protests across Europe as thousands rally for better pensions
item.description: Pensioners are marching in Madrid on Saturday to demand decent pensions, indexation to inflation and an end to the gender gap, as parallel rallies in France and Italy prompt tighter security.

item.title: Soldiers patrol Milan streets as shops board up ahead of protests
item.description: Milan is on alert ahead of expected protests, with additional soldiers deployed and shops boarding up their windows a week after looting and clashes with police.

item.title: Clashes between French police and protesters after largely peaceful demonstrations that drew thousands
item.description: Organisers said more than 800,000 took part in demonstrations across the country, with 250,000 in Paris alone. Authorities said 410,000 demonstrated nationwide. The protests were over the high cost of living and lack of funding for education.

item.title: Tensions mount in France as thousands rally against Marine Le Pen’s National rally
item.description: The mayor of Saint-Denis, Bally Bagayoko, joined left-wing politicians and trade union leaders in Orléans as Marine Le Pen's party gathered ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
